title: The ~11 Hz mystery, measured with an encoder and two hands
question: Is the slop in the drivetrain a backlash gap or a spring — and does either explain the ~11 Hz ring?
headline: A spring, decisively (linear fit residual 0.45 against 6.80 for a constant), stiffness 2.90 N*m/rad. Against the robot's inertia reflected at the wheel that predicts a 10.7 Hz mode, against 10.6 Hz observed unbraced and 11.5 braced — from an encoder and a pair of hands, with no reference to any gyro signal.
hub_output: 100 randomized trials, both wheels held, portA 59 / portB 41

p10 slope 0.1123 deg per duty%, deflection starts at 22% duty
stiffness 1.45 N*m/rad per motor, 2.90 both -> mode 10.7 Hz
